newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AEA airlines cargo up 3.2 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: AEA airlines cargo up 3.2 pct in July.

text.p: Global freight traffic carried by West European airlines in July 1996 was up 3.2 percent on the same month last year at 1.95 billion freight tonne-kilometres, FTK, the Association of European Airlines (AEA) said.
The FTK measurement is derived by multiplying the weight of cargo carried by the distance flown.

Karl-Heinz Neumeister, secretary-general of the AEA said "The July results are a clear indicator that overcapacity is back with us both for passenger and freight, the airlines have to look very closely at the capacity on offer."
The biggest volume of traffic was transported on Europe-Far East/Australasia routes, increasing 2.6 percent on July 1995 to 718.4 million FTK.
688.7 million FTK were flown on Europe-North America air cargo routes, a fall of 2.5 percent on 1995 levels, AEA added.
Traffic on Europe-Sub-Saharan Africa routes increased by 24.9 percent to 191.3 million FTK, the highest growth rate achieved by AEA's seven cargo-handling regions.
Europe-South Atlantic routes (gateways in Brazil and south of the country) throughput increased by 18.1 percent to 115.7 million FTK.
On Europe-mid-Atlantic routes (gateways south of the United States and north of Brazil), July 1996 cargo traffic transported by Western European airlines totalled 78.5 million FTK, down ten percent

In the mid and short-haul sector, Europe-Africa/Middle East routes generated 87.3 million FTK, up 21.4 percent on July 1995 in contrast to intra-European cargo traffic which fell by 3.4 percent to 72.4 million FTK.
On global long-haul routes, AEA member airlines flew 1.79 billion FTK, an increase of 2.7 percent on the same month last year. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
